headword: {聖徳太子|しょうとくたいし}

definitions.explanation: A regent and politician of the Asuka period (574–622), credited with promoting Buddhism and Chinese culture in Japan. He was featured on Japanese banknotes for many years.

examples.japanese: {聖徳太子|しょうとくたいし}は{仏教|ぶっきょう}を{広|ひろ}めた。
{聖徳太子|しょうとくたいし}は{十七条|じゅうしちじょう}の{憲法|けんぽう}を{定|さだ}めたと{言|い}われている。
examples.english: Prince Shotoku is said to have established the Seventeen-Article Constitution.

examples.japanese: かつて{一万円札|いちまんえんさつ}には{聖徳太子|しょうとくたいし}の{肖像|しょうぞう}が{描|えが}かれていた。
examples.english: The portrait of Prince Shotoku used to appear on the ten-thousand-yen bill.

notes:
USAGE:
One of the most famous historical figures in Japan. Every Japanese person learns about 聖徳太子 in school. He was featured on multiple denominations of Japanese banknotes from 1930 to 1986, and is associated with 法隆寺 temple in Nara.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {聖徳太子|しょうとくたいし}の{時代|じだい} (the era of Prince Shotoku)
- {十七条|じゅうしちじょう}の{憲法|けんぽう} (Seventeen-Article Constitution)
- {法隆寺|ほうりゅうじ} (Horyuji temple, associated with Prince Shotoku)
